# local 0003: Compound literals in function bodies are initialized once at the start of the enclosing block

- Category: [Problems without a ticket](../../unreported.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Initialize the object of a compound literal at the place where the literal is evaluated.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The object of a compound literal in a function body is initialized once, at the start of the
innermost block around the literal. A literal whose initializer names a variable therefore gets
the value that the variable had at the start of the block. A literal under a `case` label is never
initialized, because control does not pass through the start of the body of a `switch`. The file
below was compiled with `sdcc -mmcs51 cl.c` on r17176 and run in ucsim.

```c
__xdata __at (0x7000) unsigned char res[2];

int g (unsigned char op, int x)
{
  int y = 0;

  switch (op)
    {
    case 0:
      y = x ? 4 : (int){3};
      break;
    }
  return y;
}

int m (int x)
{
  x = x + 1;
  return (int){x};
}

void main (void)
{
  res[0] = g (0, 0);            /* 3 expected */
  res[1] = m (1);               /* 2 expected */
}
```

`res` is `00 01`, where `03 02` is expected. It is `00 01` with `--model-medium`, `--model-large`,
`--stack-auto`, and `--model-large --stack-auto` too. For `g` the compiler prints warning 126 for
unreachable code and warning 84 for a variable that may be used before its initialization. The
code of `m` is a single `ret`.

Two variations were run in the same way. The loop `for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) s += (int){i + 1};`
gives 3 for `s`, where 6 is expected. The statement of `g` in a block of its own,
`case 0: { y = x ? 4 : (int){3}; } break;`, gives 3, which is correct.

## Cause

The grammar action for compound literals in `src/SDCC.y` creates an anonymous variable that has
the initializer list of the literal. `gatherImplicitVariables` in `src/SDCCast.c` appends the
variable to the declarations of the innermost block around the literal. `processBlockVars` puts
the initializers of a block's declarations in front of the first statement of the block. In the
body of a `switch`, that position is in front of the first `case` label.

This was read from the source of r17176. In the output of `--dump-ast` for `g`, the variable is
declared with its initializer in the block of the `switch` body, in front of the label of `case 0`.
The code is shared by the ports. stm8 and z80 print the two warnings for `g`. Only mcs51 was run.

## Open

C11 6.5.2.5 gives compound literals the value of an unnamed object that their initializer list
initializes. The initialization therefore has to be executed where the literal is evaluated. No
patch was written.

## Related

Bug #4145 concerns compound literals with constant initializers in other expressions. Bug #4248
concerns a second initialization of literals in the initializers of declarations. Their patches,
applied to r17176, do not change the results above.
